tagging_basis: AQA 7037 specification codes; AS units mapped to the matching A-level leaf

units.summary: Explain dynamic equilibrium in relation to the water cycle.
units.difficulty_basis: 4-mark AO1 explanation of one systems concept applied to a familiar cycle; recall.

units.summary: Analyse projected rainfall change across Africa from a map and monthly graphs.
units.difficulty_basis: 6-mark AO3 analysis of a map linked with two graphs; patterns and anomalies, no recall.

units.summary: Using a Carlisle figure and own knowledge, assess natural and human causes of the 2005 flood.
units.difficulty_basis: 6-mark AO1=2 AO2=4 short assess applying drainage basin flood knowledge to a located context.

units.summary: Assess how far water cycle processes and carbon cycle drivers are inter-related.
units.difficulty_basis: 20-mark synoptic essay (AO1=10 AO2=10) linking two cycles and reaching a judgement on the extent.

units.summary: Outline how temperature variation affects weathering in hot deserts.
units.difficulty_basis: 4-mark AO1 outline of thermal weathering; recall.

units.summary: Compare summer temperature variation in the Sahara and Sonoran deserts using two graphs.
units.difficulty_basis: 6-mark AO3 comparison of two time-series graphs; patterns and anomalies with data manipulation.

units.summary: Using a shelterbelt figure and own knowledge, assess benefits of the system in combating desertification.
units.difficulty_basis: 6-mark AO1=2 AO2=4 short assess applying sustainable response knowledge to a novel scheme.

units.summary: Assess the relative importance of water and wind in shaping desert landscapes.
units.difficulty_basis: 20-mark essay comparing two process groups and the landforms they produce; relative importance evaluation.

units.summary: Explain the concept of the sediment cell.
units.difficulty_basis: 4-mark AO1 explanation of a single systems concept at the coast; recall.

units.summary: Complete a chi-squared test on coastal flooding locations in Great Britain and interpret the result.
units.difficulty_basis: 6-mark AO3 statistical calculation and interpretation with a null hypothesis; skills-led with partial table given.

units.summary: Using a Holderness photograph and own knowledge, assess the role of mass movement in landscape development.
units.difficulty_basis: 6-mark AO1=2 AO2=4 short assess applying slumping knowledge to an unfamiliar image.

units.summary: Assess whether coastal intervention can halt natural processes that threaten communities now and in the future.
units.difficulty_basis: 20-mark to-what-extent essay with an absolute claim; weighs management against sea level change and processes.

units.summary: Explain the development of warm based glaciers.
units.difficulty_basis: 4-mark AO1 explanation of one glacier type; recall.

units.summary: Compare three US glaciers using a location map and mass balance graphs.
units.difficulty_basis: 6-mark AO3 comparison across a map and two graphs; interpretation of mass balance data.

units.summary: Using three figures on Svalbard permafrost and own knowledge, assess the potential impact of the data.
units.difficulty_basis: 6-mark AO1=2 AO2=4 short assess applying permafrost and active layer knowledge to novel data.

units.summary: Assess the relative importance of water and ice in developing landscapes of glacial deposition.
units.difficulty_basis: 20-mark essay comparing ice and meltwater roles across landforms; relative importance evaluation.

units.summary: Outline processes leading to the formation of fold mountains.
units.difficulty_basis: 4-mark AO1 outline of a plate margin landform; recall.

units.summary: Assess whether seismic events always have more widespread and severe impacts than volcanic events.
units.difficulty_basis: 9-mark to-what-extent comparison of two hazard types with an absolute claim; evaluation.

units.summary: Assess the importance of globalisation factors in supporting the response to major seismic hazards.
units.difficulty_basis: 9-mark assess (AO1=4 AO2=5) needing a synoptic link to globalisation.

units.summary: Assess how far the Park model has improved understanding and management of tropical storm impacts.
units.difficulty_basis: 20-mark essay evaluating a theoretical model against storm management; extended evaluation.

units.summary: Explain the concept of sub-climax in succession.
units.difficulty_basis: 4-mark AO1 explanation of a single concept; recall.

units.summary: Analyse climate and productivity data for two biomes to relate climate to natural vegetation.
units.difficulty_basis: 6-mark AO3 analysis of a climate graph and a data table with manipulation.

units.summary: With a tropical rainforest, evaluate the role of governance in environmental management.
units.difficulty_basis: 9-mark evaluation (AO1=4 AO2=5) requiring a synoptic link to governance.

units.summary: Analyse the role of nutrient cycling within a studied hydrosere or lithosere.
units.difficulty_basis: 9-mark extended analysis (AO1=4 AO2=5) of seral stage development; a studied example required.

units.summary: Assess whether economic development in marine ecosystems can be reconciled with sustainability.
units.difficulty_basis: 20-mark to-what-extent essay with an absolute claim; evaluates conflicting economic and conservation aims.
